Hannah was deeply troubled and provoked year after year. What burden have you carried for a long time?
Hannah poured out her soul before the Lord. What would you pour out to God today?
"The Lord remembered her." What does it mean to you that God remembers?
Hannah gave Samuel back to the Lord. What has God given you that you can offer back to him?
Hannah sang, "There is none holy like the Lord." What in her song do you want to pray?
Eli's sons treated the Lord's offering with contempt. How can we treat holy things carelessly?
Samuel ministered before the Lord as a boy. How can young people serve God?
God says, "Those who honour me I will honour." How can you honour God today?
Samuel said, "Speak, for your servant hears." How can you listen for God?
Eli accepted God's word even though it was hard. How do you respond to hard words from God?
The Lord was with Samuel and let none of his words fall to the ground. What does it look like to trust God's word?
Israel brought the ark to battle, treating it like a good-luck charm. How can we use God instead of trusting him?
Eli's heart trembled for the ark of God. What do you care about most deeply?
"The glory has departed from Israel." What would it mean to lose sight of God's glory?
Dagon fell on its face before the ark of the Lord. What does this show about false gods?
The Philistines suffered while they kept the ark. What does this show about God's holiness?
The Philistines sent the ark back with a guilt offering. How did they recognise God's hand?
The people of Beth-shemesh rejoiced to see the ark. What brings you joy about God's presence?
They asked, "Who is able to stand before the Lord, this holy God?" How does Jesus answer this?
Samuel said, "Return to the Lord with all your heart and put away foreign gods." What do you need to put away?
Israel fasted, confessed and prayed, and God answered. How can confession prepare the way for God's help?
Samuel set up a stone and called it Ebenezer: "Till now the Lord has helped us." How has the Lord helped you till now?
The people asked for a king like all the nations. Where are you tempted to be like everyone else?
God said, "They have rejected me from being king over them." What does it mean to let God be your King?
Samuel warned them what a king would take. What does this teach about putting our trust in people?
Saul set out to find donkeys and found God's purpose. How does God guide through ordinary events?
Saul said, "Am I not from the least of the tribes?" How does God choose the humble?
Samuel honoured Saul and shared God's word with him. Who has spoken God's word into your life?
Samuel anointed Saul and told him God would be with him. What does God's call bring with it?
God gave Saul another heart. What does it mean that God changes hearts?
Saul hid among the baggage. Why might we hide from what God calls us to?
The Spirit of God rushed on Saul and he rescued Jabesh-gilead. How does God use us to help others?
Saul said, "Today the Lord has worked salvation." How do you give God credit for victories?
Samuel asked if he had cheated anyone. How can you live with integrity?
Samuel said, "Far be it from me that I should sin against the Lord by ceasing to pray for you." Who could you pray for regularly?
"Consider what great things he has done for you." What great things has God done for you?
Saul offered the sacrifice himself when Samuel was late. When do you get impatient with God's timing?
God sought "a man after his own heart." What does it mean to have a heart after God's?
Jonathan said, "Nothing can hinder the Lord from saving by many or by few." What does this teach about God's power?
Saul's rash oath brought trouble. How can rash words hurt others?
The people spoke up for Jonathan. When should we speak up for what is right?
Saul did not fully obey but kept the best for himself. Where might your obedience be partial?
Saul made excuses and blamed others. Why do we justify ourselves?
"To obey is better than sacrifice." What does God want more than outward religion?
God sent Samuel to anoint a new king. How does God work quietly behind the scenes?
"Man looks on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart." How does God see you?
David, the youngest, was out with the sheep. What does this show about whom God chooses?
David's music refreshed Saul. How can your gifts bring comfort to others?
Goliath defied Israel and they were afraid. What "giant" frightens you?
David said, "The Lord who delivered me from the lion... will deliver me." How do past rescues build your faith?
David refused Saul's armour and used what he knew. How can you serve God as yourself?
David said, "The battle is the Lord's." What battle do you need to give to the Lord?
Jonathan loved David as his own soul. What does loyal friendship look like?
Saul grew jealous when the women praised David. How does jealousy poison the heart?
David had success because the Lord was with him. How does God's presence shape your life?
Jonathan spoke up for David to his father. How can you stand up for a friend?
Michal helped David escape. How does God use others to protect us?
God's Spirit came upon Saul's messengers and even Saul. What does this show about God's power?
Jonathan and David made a covenant of friendship before the Lord. How can friendships be grounded in God?
Jonathan was hurt by his father's anger. How do you handle conflict in family?
David and Jonathan wept and parted in peace. How can you honour friendships through hard times?
David ate the holy bread. How does Jesus use this story to show mercy?
David pretended to be mad out of fear. What do we do when we're afraid?
Those in distress, debt and discontent gathered to David. How does this picture Jesus gathering the needy?
Saul killed the priests of Nob. What does this show about how far jealousy can go?
David said, "Stay with me; do not be afraid." How can you offer safety to others?
David asked the Lord before acting. How often do you ask God before making decisions?
"Saul sought him every day, but God did not give him into his hand." How has God protected you?
Jonathan strengthened David's hand in God. Who could you strengthen in God?
David spared Saul in the cave. What does David's restraint teach you?
David let God be the judge. How can you leave justice to God?
Saul wept and admitted David was more righteous. What can kindness do to a hard heart?
David was ready to take revenge on Nabal. What makes you want revenge?
Abigail humbly stepped in and stopped David from bloodshed. How can you be a peacemaker?
David thanked God for Abigail's wise words. How do you respond when someone corrects you?
God dealt with Nabal. What does this show about leaving vengeance to God?
David again refused to harm Saul. Why does he respect the Lord's anointed?
Saul said, "I have acted foolishly." What does true change look like?
David said in his heart, "I shall now perish." When have you felt hopeless?
David lived among the Philistines and deceived Achish. How does fear lead to compromise?
Saul sought a medium because God was silent. Where do people turn when God seems quiet?
Saul was terrified. What does this show about the cost of turning from God?
The Philistine commanders did not trust David. How did God protect David from a difficult situation?
David was sent away from the battle. How does God sometimes close doors to protect us?
David was greatly distressed, but he strengthened himself in the Lord his God. How can you strengthen yourself in the Lord?
David asked the Lord before pursuing. How do you seek God in a crisis?
David shared the spoil with those who stayed behind. What does this teach about generosity and fairness?
Saul's life ended in tragedy. What lessons does his life teach you?
The men of Jabesh-gilead honoured Saul's body. How can you show gratitude to those who helped you?
